iep101.heading: IEP 101
iep101.subtitle: Everything you need to know, in plain language
iep101.whatIsBody: An Individualized Education Program is a legally binding document that outlines the special education services your child will receive. Think of it as your child's educational roadmap — it describes where they are now, where they're headed, and how they'll get there.
iep101.whoGetsBody: Children aged 3-21 who have a disability that affects their learning. There are 13 categories under IDEA (the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act), including autism, specific learning disabilities, speech/language impairments, and more. Your child must be evaluated and found eligible before an IEP can be created.
iep101.presentLevelsText: How your child is currently doing academically and functionally
iep101.annualGoalsText: Measurable targets for the year (these should be SMART — Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound)
iep101.servicesText: What support your child will receive (speech therapy, OT, tutoring, etc.)
iep101.accommodationsText: Changes to how your child learns or is tested (extra time, preferential seating, etc.)
iep101.placementText: Where your child receives services (general education classroom, resource room, etc.)
iep101.right1: You are an equal member of the IEP team
iep101.right2: You must give consent before evaluations and services begin
iep101.right3: You have the right to see all records related to your child
iep101.right4: The school must give you Prior Written Notice before making changes
iep101.right5: You can disagree — and there are formal processes to resolve disputes (mediation, due process)
iep101.meetingHeading: What to Expect at an IEP Meeting
iep101.meetingBody: The meeting typically lasts 1-2 hours. The team reviews your child's progress, discusses goals for the coming year, and decides on services and placement. You can bring anyone you want to support you — an advocate, family member, or friend.
iep101.termRelatedServicesDef: Support services like speech, OT, PT, counseling
iep101.termTransitionDef: Planning for life after high school (starts at age 16)
iep101.termPwnDef: Written notification the school must provide before changing your child's program
iep101.termDueProcessDef: A formal hearing to resolve disagreements
